 "cells": [
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "04b28400-452c-4949-8097-b43cc66aac3e",
   "metadata": {
    "deletable": true,
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "slide"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "# 20261112 - Parallel Distribution"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "2d4ed563-df39-47cb-8d18-923a2b5f5cab",
   "metadata": {
    "deletable": true,
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "slide"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "### What does this mean? *(Copied from distributed memory parallelism notes)*\n",
    "1. We should reduce the total amount of communications necessary (*not* necessarily require less data communicated)\n",
    "    - Choose algorithms that are *communication avoiding*\n",
    "    - Remove any unnecessary communications, particularly in \"hot loops\"\n",
    "   "
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "0f6e440a-33a2-44c5-adbe-741ce00d48c5",
   "metadata": {
    "deletable": true,
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "fragment"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "2. We should \"hide\" the latency if we can\n",
    "    - Overlap communication with other useful work\n",
    "    - Computing while communicating\n",
    "    - Batching communication together (where it makes sense)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "e15c48fe-7425-4f1c-a718-7583472b85ae",
   "metadata": {
    "deletable": true,
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "slide"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "## Advice from Bill Gropp (father of MPI)\n",
    "\n",
    ">   You want to think about how you decompose your data structures, how\n",
    "    you think about them globally.  [...]  If you were building a house,\n",
    "    you'd start with a set of blueprints that give you a picture of what\n",
    "    the whole house looks like.  You wouldn't start with a bunch of\n",
    "    tiles and say. \"Well I'll put this tile down on the ground, and\n",
    "    then I'll find a tile to go next to it.\"  But all too many people\n",
    "    try to build their parallel programs by creating the smallest\n",
    "    possible tiles and then trying to have the structure of their code\n",
    "    emerge from the chaos of all these little pieces.  You have to have\n",
    "    an organizing principle if you're going to survive making your code\n",
    "    parallel.\n",
    "    -- https://www.rce-cast.com/Podcast/rce-28-mpich2.html"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "e1cc125b-2cea-42d0-a958-1ac339c62570",
   "metadata": {
    "deletable": true,
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "fragment"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "- Distributed-memory parallelism lives and dies by how you distribute the memory (duh)\n",
    "- Often needs to be done at an architectural level\n",
    "    - Can't really start piece-by-piece\n",
    "    - Difficult to take a shared memory code and make an **optimal** MPI/distributed memory program without significant modifications"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "5061ddfb-6ea6-4b89-acdd-e0a5b8739c67",
   "metadata": {
    "deletable": true,
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "slide"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "## How do we want to distribute our problem across multiple ranks?\n",
    "Two goals:\n",
    "- Distribute the total computation evenly across processors\n",
    "    - We're only as fast as the slowest process\n",
    "- Minimize communication as much as possible\n",
    "    - Both in number of communciation and amount of data to be communicated"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "7ffe8224-a8a4-4963-914b-dbbe305ec8da",
   "metadata": {
    "deletable": true,
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "slide"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "### Simplest example: Sparse matrix-vector multiply"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "2feb1605-1eb2-4b47-ad51-795ad991f577",
   "metadata": {
    "deletable": true,
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "fragment"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "Say we have a (sparse) matrix that we want to have distributed across ranks.\n",
    "- How should we distribute the matrix?\n",
    "- How should we distribute the vector?"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "873aa4f9-b516-4db0-b9f4-d605e3459f4a",
   "metadata": {
    "deletable": true,
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "slide"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "Easiest way is to parallelize by\n",
    "- Assigning rows of the vector and matrix to each rank\n",
    "- Each rank holds the matrix entries for those rows\n",
    "![dense matvec parallel](../img/05-matvec-row-dense.png)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "attachments": {},
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "4c009201-17a6-4b32-8222-9e41fd719c15",
   "metadata": {
    "deletable": true,
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "fragment"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "See [step-by-step workout of how the mat-vec product happens](https://www.sandia.gov/app/uploads/sites/197/2022/06/CS591MH_20070913.pdf)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "attachments": {
    "84fd74f3-63b2-419c-aaf6-15bbb95e462d.png": {
     "image/png": ""
    }
   },
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "2ddfe7db-ef34-4f5e-a704-d884cd9a7d4f",
   "metadata": {
    "deletable": true,
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": ""
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "![image.png](attachment:84fd74f3-63b2-419c-aaf6-15bbb95e462d.png)\n",
    "\n",
    "from [*Verification Challenges in Sparse Matrix Vector\n",
    "Multiplication in High Performance Computing: Part I*](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.13427v1)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "4ba8823c-c989-43aa-8294-3b2319734e78",
   "metadata": {
    "deletable": true,
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "slide"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "### Example matrix\n",
    "![cuthill-mckee reordering](../img/cuthill-mckee-reordering-original.png)\n",
    "\n",
    "*from [*RCM++:Reverse Cuthill-McKee ordering with Bi-Criteria Node Finder*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.04171)*\n",
    "\n",
    "- First few ranks recieve small (contiguous) portion of the vector\n",
    "    - Probably only has to communicate with one rank\n",
    "    - Very possibly doesn't have to communciate with any ranks at all (vector entries are collocated with matrix entries)\n",
    "- Next few ranks recieve many different small portions from different areas of the vector\n",
    "    - Requires recieving communication from many different ranks"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "b9782b4c-a068-4bb4-b14c-5dd7b29719b3",
   "metadata": {
    "deletable": true,
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "fragment"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "**The amount of data which needs to be transfered is dependent on the layout of the matrix**"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "d3c4f72a-5ac3-4a96-bd9e-8f2fde74ec65",
   "metadata": {
    "deletable": true,
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "slide"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "How do we fix this? \n",
    "- Just reorder the matrix entries\n",
    "    - If we apply a permutation to the rows and columns of the matrix, and to the vector, the result is identical"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "3c428783-4ac3-40f8-ad85-1bb255c7290e",
   "metadata": {
    "deletable": true,
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "slide"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "One reordering method is to use the [CutHill-McKee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuthill%E2%80%93McKee_algorithm) algorithm\n",
    "- Reduces the \"bandwidth\" of the matrix\n",
    "    - e.g. the maximum \"distance\" between non-zero entries of a row\n",
    "    \n",
    "![cuthill-mckee reordering](../img/cuthill-mckee-reordering-reordered.png)\n",
    "\n",
    "*from [*RCM++:Reverse Cuthill-McKee ordering with Bi-Criteria Node Finder*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.04171)*"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "bbfee412-e754-46bf-856b-6be0f5743da0",
   "metadata": {
    "deletable": true,
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "slide"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "Another way to reorder to use graph-based partitioners\n",
    "- Examples are ParMeTiS, PTSCOTCH, or Chaco\n",
    "- These interpret the non-zero pattern of the matrix as a graph via an [adjacency matrix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adjacency_matrix)\n",
    "- The graph is then split into subsets of nodes, while trying to minimize edge cuts\n",
    "- Edges can be weighted favor some edge cuts over others\n",
    "    - For matrices, mostly interesting for parallel preconditioning performance (e.g. performance of additive Schwartz methods)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "5efadf9e-07f1-442c-bdbc-deb83578d5ee",
   "metadata": {
    "deletable": true,
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "fragment"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "- Graph partitioning usually better than \"naive\" Cuthill-McKee application\n",
    "    - It tries to directly solve the problem\n",
    "    - But the problem to be solved isn't possible to solve exactly\n",
    "    - Literally NP-complete problem"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "43c01455-0a12-44e7-b38b-de85607c3068",
   "metadata": {
    "deletable": true,
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "slide"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "## Physical domain partitioning (domain decomposition)\n",
    "\n",
    "- For many scientific problems, governed by partial differential equations (PDEs)\n",
    "- Defined on a domain, which is then discretized (split into finite parts)\n",
    "- How we split these apart matters\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "7a965302-272b-412b-899c-c8320664ed2b",
   "metadata": {
    "deletable": true,
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "slide"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "### Example: finite different, 5 point stencil\n",
    "\n",
    "- Take domain (large rectangle) and discretize evenly into rows and columns of points\n",
    "- We partition those points into small blocks\n",
    "- Each parallel process \"holds\" one partition\n",
    "\n",
    "![parallel split of FD grid](../img/stencil-parallel-Eijkhout.png)\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "3df82e7d-467c-41be-98d3-cc962f71a351",
   "metadata": {
    "deletable": true,
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "slide"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "- To compute the stencil, we need the points to the left, right, top, and bottom of each point we have\n",
    "- At the edge, these needed points are owned by other processes\n",
    "- So we need to communicate them somehow"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "d71863bb-26c4-4801-972f-e8324956abbe",
   "metadata": {
    "deletable": true,
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "slide"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "- On each rank, we create a \"halo\" ring of points we need, but we do not own\n",
    "    - Sometimes also called ghost cells, rind, or shared points\n",
    "- These halo points them must be communicated around\n",
    "\n",
    "![parallel halo of FD grid](../img/stencil-halo-Eijkhout.png)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "ea433963-6ff5-4de6-a4e8-438b27e5acea",
   "metadata": {
    "deletable": true,
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "slide"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "### More detailed example:\n",
    "\n",
    "Same example as before, just more noisy (but more realistic)\n",
    "\n",
    "![FEM partitioning](../img/FEM-partitioning-nakajima.png)\n",
    "\n",
    "*from *Parallel Iterative Solvers of GeoFEM with Selective Blocking Preconditioning for Nonlinear Contact Problems on the Earth Simulator* by Kengo Nakajima*"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "c5d14f44-c7dc-4138-8fca-69562639a4db",
   "metadata": {
    "deletable": true,
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "slide"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "![FEM partitioning](../img/FEM-partition-communication-nakajima.png)\n",
    "*from *Parallel Iterative Solvers of GeoFEM with Selective Blocking Preconditioning for Nonlinear Contact Problems on the Earth Simulator* by Kengo Nakajima*"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "932eea8b-0f84-4761-85a4-bf605a2d8a3f",
   "metadata": {
    "deletable": true,
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "slide"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "### How do we split the domain?\n",
    "- What we do we want in our partitioning?\n",
    "    - This can sometimes change depending on what problem you're doing, what algorithms you use, etc.\n",
    "- Generally:\n",
    "    - Give each rank approximately the same amount of \"owned\" data (analgous to how much work each rank does)\n",
    "    - Reduce the communication between them"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "b281f2a3-5248-4c13-b20a-01842e122453",
   "metadata": {
    "deletable": true,
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "fragment"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "- The physical way of thinking about this is to evenly distribute volume, while minimizing surface area for each rank\n",
    "    - Volume kinda equals the total amount of points in a partition\n",
    "    - Surface area kinda means the amount of communication that needs to be done\n",
    "- The partitions, physically, should look \"ball-like\"\n",
    "    - Obviously not possible for every partition, otherwise there would be gaps (see [packing factor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sphere_packing))"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "f1c13c10-cc32-43ff-ac8a-8dd4b638d149",
   "metadata": {
    "deletable": true,
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "slide"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "Again, we use graph partitioners to do this\n",
    "- Graph describes the connectivity between each point\n",
    "- Graph partitioner creates even subsets (partitions) while minimizing edge cut of the graph\n",
    "- Example partitioners: ParMETIS, PTSCOTCH, etc."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "c63365a3-1d87-4f37-8827-041b610b5356",
   "metadata": {
    "deletable": true,
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "slide"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "### Matrices based on Physical Domain\n",
    "- If we want to create a matrix based on the physical domain discretization, do we need to do more partitioning?\n",
    "- Not really...\n",
    "    - The graph used for domain partitioning is usually heavily related (if not identical) to the graph used for matrix partitioning\n",
    "    - We normally just use the row or column -based matrix partitioning method after that"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "50e95435-cc02-4e16-ac0c-912878082fa5",
   "metadata": {
    "deletable": true,
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "slide"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "## Hierarchical Partitioning\n",
    "\n",
    "- As previously discussed, not all communication is equal\n",
    "    - Intra NUMA $\\neq$ inter NUMA $\\neq$ inter compute node $\\neq$ inter-rack (networking)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "1f083aad-88fb-47c5-b05c-cb73340bc629",
   "metadata": {
    "deletable": true,
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "fragment"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "- Thus, for partitioning work, some edge cuts are not the same as others\n",
    "    - We want to minimize edge cuts between nodes more than we want to minimize overall\n",
    "- Can't use the normal edge weights of graph partitioners\n",
    "    - These weights are about the graph itself\n",
    "    - We care about the *partitions*\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "f5abbb96-a1c6-4478-827a-561602f49cc3",
   "metadata": {
    "deletable": true,
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "slide"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "Solution is hierarchical partitioning\n",
    "- Split matrix/domain into partitions, one for each compute node\n",
    "- Then split those compute node partitions\n",
    "\n",
    "Example: If we have 6 compute nodes, with 12 cores each, then\n",
    "- Partition into 6 chunks\n",
    "    - This minimizes the communication cuts between nodes\n",
    "- Partition each of the 6 chunks into 12 sub-chunks\n",
    "    - This minimizes the communication within each node\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "d7231d43-82a3-4b7f-99fc-b160cd826dd8",
   "metadata": {
    "deletable": true,
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "slide"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "Can do this on higher levels too\n",
    "- Partition for each rack, then each node, then individual cores"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "71d198e4-dffc-4405-90ea-8438f031d9c4",
   "metadata": {
    "deletable": true,
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "fragment"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "Important for multi-GPU too\n",
    "- Recall the communication networks on the same node between GPUs"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "3ac9ac36-1b28-46ed-945e-656d5db94a8b",
   "metadata": {
    "deletable": true,
    "editable": true,
    "slideshow": {
     "slide_type": "slide"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "source": [
    "![hierarchical partition matrix-vector product](https://sandialabs.github.io/Zoltan/ug_html/Structural_MATVEC_Avg_Time.jpg)\n",
    "\n",
    "*From [Zoltan guide](https://sandialabs.github.io/Zoltan/ug_html/ug_alg_hier.html)*"
   ]
  },
